Keep the video if you want to show it off, but the demo field needs to be the runnable thing plus a short README explaining how to run it. The problem is scope versus the 27 hours logged: the project is a single static page (one index.html plus script.js and style.css) that runs a Pomodoro countdown with a looping gif and a couple of sound files, and the repo at https://github.com/PIXEL-169/StudyDojo only has 11 commits, none of which reflect anywhere near 27 hours of building. A timer with a gif and a few buttons is a real start, but the logged time and the amount of actual code don't line up, and the lack of a commit history to back up that time is what we can't approve. For your next project, commit early and often as you build so your git history tells the story of the hours you spent, and aim for something with enough features to genuinely fill the time you log. Per the YSWS rules (https://hack.club/ysws-rules), this can't be resubmitted.
